newsitem.title: USA: McDonnell plant to convert Fedex DC-1.
newsitem.headline: McDonnell plant to convert Fedex DC-1.

text.p: McDonnell Douglas said it will set up a conversion facility near Phoenix to do most of the work rebuilding DC-10 passenger jets as MD-10 freighters for Federal Express Corp.
Under the initial contract, Douglas will do conversions on at least 12 DC-10s for FedEx at the Goodyear site, the company said.
FedEx is buying the DC-10-10 passenger jets from American Airlines and United Airlines. Douglas has a contract to convert up to 60 DC-10s for FedEx, which will be redesignated as MD-10s.
Douglas said it has a separate contract with Dimension Aviation for converting MD-11 passenger jets to freighters for Federal Express. That work also begins this month at the Goodyear site.
The first three MD-10 conversions are due to be completed by next fall, and then continue at regular intervals into 2000, the company said.
Additionally, FedEx is expected to award a contract to Douglas to install a two-person flight deck on each MD-10.
At peak production, about 475 aircraft mechanics, supervisors and support personnel will be employed on the MD-10 project. Additional staff will be hired for the MD-11 conversions, the company said.
Alenia, a unit of Italy's state-controlled engineering group has been selected by McDonnell as a second source for the DC-10 conversions.
On March 6, Alenia announced it had signed an agreement with McDonnell for the firm conversion of 13 DC-10s into freighters with options on a further 30.
